title: Provision and Monsoon
premise: Desert ranger Juniper Vane has spent a decade chasing petty thieves across the empty miles, content to be forgotten. When dying prospector Elias Marsh trades him a map to the river's forbidden source for a promise—that Juniper will deliver the truth about who poisoned the water towns along the river—Juniper is pulled into a conspiracy run by the very magistrate who once pardoned him. Pursued by his former partner Sera Quill, bound by duty to bring him in, and accompanied by the thief he was originally hunting, Wren Calloway, Juniper must reach the source before the dry season seals it forever. In the end, Juniper exposes the magistrate's crime at the cost of his own freedom, choosing truth over invisibility and finding that loyalty, rightly placed, and love are not duties to be weighed but the same thing.
about_author: Felix Eriksen is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons running cargo through drought-stricken canyon country before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about landscapes that punish hesitation and people who refuse to disappear.

chapters.title: The Man Who Measured in Miles
chapters.summary: Juniper Vane's POV. Ten years of tracking thieves across the flats have made him a ghost with a badge; he catches Wren Calloway mid-theft but hesitates when she claims she stole only a letter. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Prospector Elias Marsh, poisoned and dying at a waystation, trades Juniper a map to the river's forbidden source for a promise: carry the truth downstream. Emotional beat: the weight of a promise accepted before its price is known.

chapters.title: What Wren Stole
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The stolen letter names Magistrate Corven Hale as the man diverting the river's headwaters—and poisoning towns that resist. Wren bargains her freedom for partnership. Emotional beat: wary alliance between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: Downstream Towns
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the settlement of Dry Hollow, Juniper sees children sick from tainted water and realizes Elias's poison was no accident. Emotional beat: guilt—the ranger who policed theft while murder went unpunished.

chapters.title: Sera
chapters.summary: Sera Quill's POV. Juniper's former partner arrives with a warrant, torn between the law she serves and the man she once trusted. She lets them go one night, then regrets it. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a rope.

chapters.title: The River Turns Against You
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following the map upstream, the trio survives a flash flood that destroys their supplies and nearly drowns Wren. Emotional beat: the land as antagonist; trust forged in shared survival.

chapters.title: Hale's Men
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Magistrate Hale's riders ambush them at a ferry crossing; an old boatman dies covering their escape. Emotional beat: the cost of the promise begins coming due, and Juniper stops pretending it's just a job.

chapters.title: Canyon of Names
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Sheltering in a canyon wall carved with prospectors' marks—including Elias's—they find his hidden cache: ledgers proving Hale bought the water rights with bribed judges. Emotional beat: hope hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Pardon
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera confronts Juniper alone; he reveals the pardon she helped arrange ten years ago was Hale's leash on him. She must choose whose justice she serves. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed—loyalty vs. truth inside one person.

chapters.title: Dry Season Rising
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With weeks left before the dry season closes the high passes, they push through salt flats; Wren's fevered collapse forces a brutal choice between speed and care. Emotional beat: love surfacing against duty, unspoken.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At a toll bridge garrisoned by Hale's men, Sera appears—arresting Juniper publicly while secretly passing him the garrison's route codes. Emotional beat: sacrifice performed as betrayal.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Mile Markers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Held overnight, Juniper faces Hale himself, who offers him his old life back if he surrenders the ledgers. Emotional beat: temptation of invisibility—the easy lie he's lived for a decade.

chapters.title: Breakout at First Light
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Sera, uneasy allies now, spring Juniper from the garrison; Sera burns her warrant openly, becoming a fugitive too. Emotional beat: three loyalties aligning against one corrupt law.

chapters.title: The Ascent Begins
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They enter the gorge country where the map grows cryptic; rockfalls close the low route behind them, making retreat impossible. Emotional beat: commitment past the point of return.

chapters.title: Ghost Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They find an abandoned diversion camp—Hale's crews dammed the source years ago—and evidence of workers killed to keep the secret. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Sera's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Ambushed by her own former deputies, Sera holds a pass alone so the others can climb on; wounded, she sends word ahead instead of following. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with blood.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the forbidden source—a spring sealed behind Hale's dam—they find Elias's final testimony carved in stone and the last proof needed. Emotional beat: awe and terrible clarity; the promise nearly kept.

chapters.title: Breaking the Dam
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. To free the water and prove the crime physically, they breach the dam as Hale's riders arrive; the flood carries the evidence downstream toward the towns. Emotional beat: climax—truth unleashed, literally.

chapters.title: Standoff at the High Ledge
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Cornered above the flooding gorge, Juniper refuses to shoot Hale's captain, instead letting the rising water and arriving townspeople force surrender. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, delivered without becoming the thing he hunts.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Carrying the wounded Wren downriver, Juniper passes the towns drinking clean water again, children recovering. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; the miles finally feel like they lead somewhere.

chapters.title: Judgment at Dry Hollow
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Hale stands trial before the towns he poisoned; Juniper testifies, surrendering his badge and accepting charges for the breakout. Emotional beat: accountability embraced—loyalty to truth over self-preservation.

chapters.title: Provision and Monsoon
chapters.summary: Juniper and Wren's alternating POV. Released to community service as the season's first monsoon breaks, Juniper plants his mile markers in the ground for good and stays. Emotional beat: resolution—love chosen over wandering, home measured in people, not miles.
